$comment: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 contributors. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. The spec format, kinds board, soc, chip, ip, overlay, facts, peripheral and review (SF2-7). Design: docs/SPEC-FORMAT.md. Patterns end with (?![\s\S]) (nothing follows), never $: in Python's re, which the validator uses, $ also matches before a final newline, so an id "w\n" would pass. The lookahead means end of string in Python and ECMA-262 alike. Optional lists are absent or non-empty, except topology provider endpoint cells (an empty array explicitly carries zero values).
title: Spec format: a spec or an investigator's facts file

then.$comment: An overlay's sections are its target's; which target kind is the checker's to know (SF2-2), so the schema admits the union of the board-spec kinds' sections.

describes.$comment: The soc, chip or board specs whose block this peripheral spec programs: structural composition, like parts, so outside every fact's basis and not license-gated.

then.$comment: message: resetTypes, fieldAccessPolicyDefinitions, enumerationDefinitions and registerFiles belong to a peripheral, an overlay or a facts file, not to this kind
message: resetTypes, fieldAccessPolicyDefinitions and registerFiles belong to a peripheral, an overlay or a facts file, not to this kind (enumerationDefinitions is allowed)

text.$comment: Free text: a string with at least one character that is not white space.

line.$comment: Single-line text: words separated by single spaces; no leading, trailing or doubled space, no newline.

name.$comment: A resources entry name (document or repository), also used for cache names.

date.$comment: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD; February 29 only in leap years.

gitRef.$comment: A git ref name for a map-only repos entry: no leading '-', no white space or shell metacharacters, none of git's forbidden forms (.., //, a component starting with '.', a trailing '/' or '.', .lock; @{ cannot occur, as the character set has no braces), no leading '+' (a refspec's force flag), and not 40 or 64 hex digits in either case (that is a commit, written as commit).

symbol.$comment: A symbol, macro, label or property name as the source spells it, C++ and assembler included (~Foo, operator<<, Foo<T>, ns::Class::method, $label, struct gic_chip_data): single-line, no leading '-', no leading, trailing or doubled space. Orchestrator decision 2026-10-08. It reaches a command line (SF2-6) only as a separate argument after --, never through a shell.

dtNode.$comment: A device-tree node name or path: no leading '-', no white space or shell metacharacters.

method.$comment: How something was fetched (via, fetch_via): prose for a reader, never executed by any tool. Single-line, no leading '-'; parentheses and apostrophes allowed; no ; | & $ backquote backslash < > (orchestrator decision 2026-10-08).

hex.$comment: One spelling for a hex value (D6): 0x, lowercase digits, no separators, no leading zeros (0x0 for zero). No type here, so a nullable field can use it.

httpsUrl.$comment: https only; a host of DNS labels (no user information, no empty or hyphen-edged label), a port from 1 to 65535; no white space or backslash; nothing else reaches a tool (RG-T1 R1).

path.$comment: A path inside a repository: relative, no empty, '.', '..' or '.git' segment, no leading '-', no '~', a trailing '/' for a directory.

filePath.$comment: A path naming a file: a path without the trailing '/' of a directory.

spdxExpression.$comment: An SPDX expression; the checker parses it (board-expert/scripts/spdx.py).

critical.$comment: Omit the key for a fact that is not critical.

supportRules.$comment: For anything that carries support: a fact, an instance row, a variant row.

anyOf.$comment: a correspondence fact's pair anchors are its support; instance and variant rows have no section and never match
message: a gap (no support) must carry a todo

then.$comment: message: press, inference, emulated and extension-class support require a todo

support.$comment: message: an inference stands alone in support; cite the read part as its own fact (D3)
message: emulated never stands alone; another class must support the claim beside it

instance.$comment: One placement of a block in an SoC or chip; verified like a fact. It names the block's ip spec, its peripheral spec, or both. reg and irq are null when unknown, and then the row carries a todo.

allOf.$comment: message: an instance names an ip spec, a peripheral spec, or both

then.$comment: message: an instance with reg or irq null must carry a todo

irq.$comment: null when unknown (the row then carries a todo); otherwise the GIC line, or the line on a secondary controller.

support.$comment: One support entry. class is a closed enum; each class declares its own fields in its branch, so a field of another class is unevaluated and refused.

allOf.$comment: standard and doc: a heading alone is admitted here. Orchestrator decision 2026-10-08: a databook always needs a precise locator (preciseLocator); a standard needs one only when its document entry has pages (a paged document), which SF2-2's checker enforces, since the schema cannot see the document entry from the citation.

readSupport.$comment: A support entry of any class but inference: a premise's or a conflict's support. A conclusion another fact needs is its own inference fact, referenced by id.

class.$comment: message: a premise's support is read, never another inference; reference an inference fact instead

premise.$comment: Exactly one of: a fact reference (with optional uses), a states text with its own read support, or a named assumption.

locator.$comment: Where in a document. All values are strings; pages is [first, last]; page and pages never together.

preciseLocator.$comment: A databook locator: a heading alone is not enough (RG1 V2).

allOf.$comment: message: a databook locator needs a section, page, pages, table, figure or clause

lines.$comment: [first, last], 1-based, inclusive; first <= last is the checker's (SF2-2).

srcAnchor.$comment: lines and symbol, or search alone (a negative or global claim).

then.$comment: message: a search anchor carries no lines, symbol, comment or stale

dtAnchor.$comment: lines for a source .dts/.dtsi; node for a decompiled blob; both allowed.

resources.$comment: Absent or non-empty: {} would be a second spelling of an absent key.

access.$comment: message: access is public, registration, members-only or private (internal was renamed private)

cite.$comment: A map-only document: citing it is an error. Omit the key otherwise.

repo.$comment: A pin: a full commit, or a branch in ref for a map-only entry; never both.

attribution.$comment: Source copyright attribution declared by the file's notices at the pinned commit (#101). Absent means not recorded. Checked by resolve; bookkeeping for freshness.

series.$comment: An unmerged patch series: a map, never cited.

tool.$comment: Declarative: what exists and which skill drives it (via).

via.$comment: the skill that drives the tool

assessment.$comment: Used by review payloads in SF2-7b, not a verification verdict.

registryName.$comment: A name in one of a spec's registries (resetTypes, fieldAccessPolicyDefinitions, enumerationDefinitions, registerFiles), as the standard or the document spells it: RW1CS, power-on, link-width.

fieldRef.$comment: A field of a register fact in the same file: #<fact id>.<field id>.

quantity.$comment: A measured or specified amount (D27): a UCUM code and IEC 61360 level names. Values are decimal integers (D6 keeps floats out); the unit list selects codes and copies none of UCUM's tables.

allOf.$comment: message: a quantity needs a unit and at least one of min, nom, typ, max

timeQuantity.$comment: A quantity in a time unit with no level below 0: a step's timeout, interval and duration.

unit.$comment: message: a step's timeout, interval and duration are times: unit s, ms, us, ns, min or h, and no level below 0

min.$comment: message: a step's timeout, interval and duration are times: unit s, ms, us, ns, min or h, and no level below 0

nom.$comment: message: a step's timeout, interval and duration are times: unit s, ms, us, ns, min or h, and no level below 0

typ.$comment: message: a step's timeout, interval and duration are times: unit s, ms, us, ns, min or h, and no level below 0

max.$comment: message: a step's timeout, interval and duration are times: unit s, ms, us, ns, min or h, and no level below 0

stepTarget.$comment: message: a step target is #<fact id> or #<fact id>.<field id> in the same file

stepValue.$comment: Canonical hex or an enumerated value's name; the checker sorts them out.

ipxactAccess.$comment: IEEE 1685-2022 accessType, spelled as the standard spells it (D24).

writeValueConstraint.$comment: message: writeValueConstraint is exactly one of {writeAsRead: true}, {useEnumeratedValues: true} or {minimum, maximum}

access.$comment: The six IP-XACT values, and the six legacy short values the checker warns about (LEGACY_ACCESS in peripheral.py).

then.$comment: message: a register with a legacy short access (ro, wo, rw, w1c, w1s, rc) may not also carry modifiedWriteValue or readAction; write the IP-XACT access

allOf.$comment: message: a field has its own enumeratedValues or an enumerationDefinitionRef, not both

then.$comment: message: a field that names a fieldAccessPolicyDefinitionRef may not also set access, modifiedWriteValue, readAction, writeValueConstraint or unaffectedBy; the policy holds them

allOf.$comment: message: a layout field has its own enumeratedValues or an enumerationDefinitionRef, not both

until.$comment: message: until is exactly one of equals, bitsSet or bitsClear

then.$comment: message: a step with op has no action: the renderer writes its English; explanations go in note (D40)

allOf.$comment: message: target, value, mask, until, interval, timeout, duration and onTimeout belong to a step with op
message: onTimeout needs a timeout
message: a write step needs target and value
message: a write step takes only target, value besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a setBits step needs target
message: a setBits step takes only mask, target besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a clearBits step needs target
message: a clearBits step takes only mask, target besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a read step needs target
message: a read step takes only target besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a poll step needs target and until
message: a poll step takes only interval, onTimeout, target, timeout, until besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a poll or waitInterrupt step needs a timeout, or a todo saying the source gives none (#105)
message: a delay step needs duration
message: a delay step takes only duration besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a waitInterrupt step needs target
message: a waitInterrupt step takes only onTimeout, target, timeout besides id, requirement, support, todo and note
message: a poll or waitInterrupt step needs a timeout, or a todo saying the source gives none (#105)

resolution.$comment: The status branches also reject every non-object; an extra object type guard would be redundant.
